correctness.rationale: Vertex constraints dominate all boundary constraints for polytopes. Summing them gives the lower bound \(f_0(P)/lpha(P)\), while symmetry averaging gives equality for vertex-transitive \(P\). Polarity identifies \(lpha(P)\) with the number of dual facets in an open central halfspace. Exact exhaustive antipodal-transversal certificates give \(lpha(D)=5\) and \(lpha(I)=3\). For \(i(D)\), four directions would force four disjoint maximal five-sets; all 495 possibilities fail, while five explicit halfspaces cover the dual facets.

value.rationale: The regular dodecahedron and icosahedron are canonical centrally symmetric three-dimensional test bodies for illumination. Exact fractional values provide benchmark data beyond the cube and octahedron, and the dodecahedron exhibits a clean integrality gap \(5/4\) between ordinary and fractional direction covers. The vertex-transitive formula is reusable structural information rather than a single numerical lookup.
risks: The result is confined to two Platonic solids and does not classify fractional illumination for all vertex-transitive polytopes.
